newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Blue chip losses halt Prague bourse's advance.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip losses halt Prague bourse's advance.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange's four-session advancing streak ground to a halt on Monday, with losses to several blue chips pulling the PX50 index down 1.4 points to 513.1.

Most of the bourse's major issues -- including SPT Telecom, CEZ, Komercni Banka, Chemopetrol and Ceska Sporitelna -- lost ground on the day, and dealers said they saw little reason for a sustained upturn in the bourse.
Overall on the bourse, 117 issues rose, while 71 fell and 45 held steady. Total volume was moderate at 455,896 shares on turnover of 691.4 million crowns.

Shares of CEZ, which supplies about 75 percent of the country's power, lost six crowns on Monday to 925. Some analysts said the stock would only become attractive at more than 100 crowns lower due to a decline in power use.
"We recommend to sell CEZ shares and consider buying under the 800 level," said Pavel Capouch of Stratego Invest.

CEZ had to slash its profit forecast to between five and six billion crowns this year from original estimates of 6.1 billion crowns due to a fall in demand. Last year the firm's net profit dropped to 7.8 billion from 8.1 billion in 1995.
Demand fell 5.5 percent in the first quarter, mainly due to an economic slowdown, pushing net profit in the period down to 2.46 bilion crowns from 3.51 billion.
Meanwhile Komercni shares lost most of Friday's 106 crown gain, falling 75 crowns to 1,779.

Komercni shares jumped at the end of last week after the Bank of New York received approval from the Czech National Bank to convert another three percent of Komercni's shares into global depositary receipts (GDR).
Currently 10 percent of Komercni's shares are converted through the U.S. bank.
